title: Replace the storefront identity
question: These are new compositions, not colour edits of the current page. Choose the direction to build as a working mobile and desktop storefront. Your logo and shopping behaviour stay intact.

options.label: Market arcade
options.lineage: Neighbourhood shopping arcades and modern retail wayfinding
options.thesis: A bright shopping destination with distinct departments and bold campaign windows.
options.viewport: Desktop: a department rail beside two campaign windows; mobile: one bold campaign, photo departments and immediate product cards.
options.risk: Needs restrained campaign content to avoid becoming a noisy offers page.

raised.raise: Keep one explicit typography hierarchy; do not carry inherited competing heading scales.
Commit colour to whole regions, rather than scattering pastel card fills.
Make horizontal browsing visible and keyboard accessible; never hide prices on hover.
Keep address, options and purchase states legible and persistent.
Use strong alignment and a deliberate measure for product information.
Preserve stable price and action alignment across cards.

options.label: Care wayfinding
options.lineage: Clear pharmacy counters and public-service wayfinding
options.thesis: A search-led care counter with a strong identity and a direct path to products.
options.viewport: Desktop: wide search-led masthead above a single campaign; mobile: address/search first, compact browse controls and two-column cards.
options.risk: More familiar retail structure; only a disciplined rebuild will keep it distinct from the rejected candidate.

options.label: Bitmap pharmacy index
options.thesis: A catalogue displayed as a type specimen.
materials: pixel display and smooth catalogue text
options.viewport: Oversized pharmacy title above dense product entries.
options.risk: Pixel display clashes with the supplied reference typography.
options.case: Pharmacy audience identification and small-screen product clarity both weaken.
options.kept: Keep one explicit typography hierarchy; do not carry inherited competing heading scales.

options.label: Care department map
options.thesis: Browse the pharmacy as a map of departments.
materials: flat colour lobes and map capsules
options.viewport: One coloured department island fills the first screen.
options.risk: Map exploration adds friction to a direct shopping task.
options.case: Audience identification and immediate product comparison lose to familiar department signage.
options.kept: Commit colour to whole regions, rather than scattering pastel card fills.

options.label: Care catalogue wall
options.thesis: A wall of product photography reveals detail on focus.
materials: focused product tiles and scrolling rails
options.viewport: Product rails fill a dark catalogue wall.
options.risk: Hidden metadata makes prices and stock harder to compare.
options.case: The media ritual is less recognisable as pharmacy shopping and obscures commerce facts.
options.kept: Make horizontal browsing visible and keyboard accessible; never hide prices on hover.

options.label: Shopping itinerary
options.thesis: The shopping journey becomes a sequence of item slips.
materials: ruled labels and connected purchase stages
options.viewport: A search coupon leads to departments and product slips.
options.risk: Travel metaphors are unrelated to everyday pharmacy shopping.
options.case: Audience identification and product clarity weaken when shopping becomes ticket handling.
options.kept: Keep address, options and purchase states legible and persistent.

options.label: Care reference index
options.thesis: A pharmacy catalogue organised as a reference work.
materials: text entries and bordered product plates
options.viewport: A shoulder index accompanies measured product entries.
options.risk: Long reading measures constrain quick mobile shopping.
options.case: Audience identification and fast visual comparison lose to the market composition.
options.kept: Use strong alignment and a deliberate measure for product information.

options.label: Live product board
options.thesis: A departure-style board compares products in rows.
materials: fixed columns and persistent stock states
options.viewport: Search and product rows lead the whole viewport.
options.risk: Board density suppresses product photos and discovery.
options.case: Pharmacy identification and pack recognition are weaker than a photo-led market.
options.kept: Preserve stable price and action alignment across cards.

canonCard.label: Conventional pharmacy retail
canonCard.thesis: The familiar pharmacy shopping pattern, rebuilt consistently.
canonCard.viewport: Search, campaign carousel, categories and a product grid.
canonCard.risk: Closest to the layout you just rejected.
